clean_old: I did a deeper analysis of the performance regression, and here's what I found. First, the regression started with the release on the 4th, not the one on the 6th like we thought, because the dashboard I was looking at averages over a week and hid it. Second, the cause is the new permissions check, which loads the full role tree from the database on every request instead of caching it per user. It adds about 30 milliseconds. Third, it only shows up on endpoints that call the check more than once, like the project list, which calls it for every row. So the fix is to cache the role tree per request and to batch the check for lists. I have a branch with the first part, and it brings the p95 back to where it was. The batching is a bigger change, so I'd split it into a separate PR. Let me know if you agree.

Subject: Proposal to adopt trunk-based development

Hi all,

I'd like to propose that we move from long-lived feature branches to trunk-based development.

The main problem today is that branches live for a week or more, so merges are painful and reviews are huge. In trunk-based development, we merge small changes to main at least daily, hide unfinished work behind feature flags, and rely on the CI pipeline to keep main always releasable.

The prerequisites are a fast and reliable test suite, which we are close to, and a flag system, which we already have.

If you're interested, I'll set up a pilot with the platform team for one month and report back.

Thank you
